note: Adapted from the species description of Acholotermes chirotus by Sands (1972), originally in English; the species has no soldier, and only the alate and the worker are described; measurement-table headings, figure numbers, distribution records and synonymy are not translated, and some measurement values corrupted by OCR in the tables are omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: This is the smallest species of the genus, distinctly smaller than A. tithasus, with which it is almost certainly sympatric. The ocelli of the alate are relatively large and closer to the compound eye, and the mandibular apical teeth are shorter in both castes. Among the two savanna species, the alate of A. epius and A. imbellis has a far more inflated postclypeus than this species; in the worker, the midgut and hindgut of A. epius overlap and the fore tibia is slender, while A. imbellis has an equally inflated postclypeus and longer apical teeth. The worker abdomen appears to be of the weakly dehiscent type.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule straw yellow, pilosity yellow, setae fairly numerous. Postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.30. Mandibular apical teeth long; ratio of left apical tooth to first marginal tooth 0.81, corresponding ratio of right mandible 1.11; left accessory marginal tooth just free of the molar prominence in surface view; composite ratio of left apical, first marginal and third marginal teeth 22.30; anterior margin of first marginal tooth of right mandible shorter than that of second marginal tooth, composite ratio 26.05. Fore tibia moderately inflated, T1/Tw 3.91; third apical spur distinct, about one third the length of the other two spurs. Midgut and hindgut meet almost transversely, to the right of the Malpighian node; enteric valve seat dorsal in the undissected abdomen; internal cushions of the enteric valve weakly developed, surface scaly, posterior margin of each scale ornamented with numerous minute spines; membranous wall of the valve beyond the cushions with numerous rather prominent spines arranged in 15–20 rows, interrupted between the cushions into fringed lobes.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule dark brown, darker above the ocelli; fontanelle very small, less than one quarter the size of an ocellus, nearly flat, circular or short oval, pale brown; middle spot equal to the fontanelle in size and shape, concolorous with the head capsule; postclypeus brown, labrum pale yellowish brown; frontal mark a dark brown flat crescent; antennae yellowish brown. Pronotum and meso- and metanotum brown, transverse sutures present but weak on the mesonotum; femora pale yellowish brown, tibiae and tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites brown, dorsolateral spiracles dark brown, sternites yellowish brown with the middle yellow, ventrolateral spiracles brown; cerci yellow. Posterior margin of head capsule broadly and evenly rounded; ocelli rather large, separated from the compound eye by only about half their own minimum diameter; postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.25–0.27, posterior margin arched and not evenly rounded, median suture distinct. Mandibular apical teeth rather long, ratio of apical to first marginal tooth 0.72–0.82, right mandible 1.05; left accessory marginal tooth just free of the molar prominence in surface view, composite ratio 12.88–14.20; first marginal tooth of right mandible inserted slightly behind the line from the apical to the second marginal tooth, anterior margins of first and second marginal teeth subequal. Head capsule pilosity dark brown, uneven, not forming a felt. Meso- and metanotum rather broad at the constriction, M/W 0.30. Third apical spur of fore tibia distinct, about one third the length of the other two spurs.
